answer: An agent economy can require every new identity to lock a refundable bond, then earn transaction limits through endorsements from trusted agents and pass random, task-specific challenges. Endorsements are weighted by the endorser’s own bonded reputation, so fresh identities cannot cheaply certify one another; detected collusion slashes the bonds. An attacker must fund each fake agent, wait to build history, and risk losing capital, whether operating from a jetty, selling saffron, or routing goods through a wharf.
